# Baghdad 830 – Electricity & electronics

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Static electricity, conductors and insulators, Leyden jar** [`static_electricity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/static_electricity.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. That rubbed amber (kahruba, 'straw-robber' in Persian) draws chaff is common knowledge. Nobody separates it from the lodestone; a dry climate makes demonstrations easy.
- **Lightning rod** [`lightning_rod`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lightning_rod.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Lightning is rare over Baghdad; in kalam it is an act of God, in Aristotle an exhalation. Minarets and domes are seldom struck, so there is little demand.
- **Electric battery (voltaic pile)** [`electric_battery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/electric_battery.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Copper, iron and silver are at hand; zinc is not isolated but brass and tutty (zinc oxide) are known. Vinegar and alum solutions serve as electrolyte. The 'Baghdad battery' jars are Parthian or Sasanian and their use is unknown.
